newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs surge after weaker-than-expected output data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs surge after weaker-than-expected output data.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract jumped more than 0.70 yen on Thursday in reaction to weaker-than-expected industrial output data for April.

The contract hit a session high of 123.55 after the data, after hovering around 122.80 just before the figures came out at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT). Japan's industrial production fell 0.4 percent in April from the previous month, compared with the Trade Ministry's earlier forecast of a 0.3 percent rise.
Earlier in the afternoon, there had been a vague rumour that the figure could be weak, dealers said.

"There was a vague rumour that the output figures could be weak. But nobody was talking about concrete figures, or nobody was sure which month the rumour was about," said a dealer at the securities unit of a city bank.

Economists polled by Reuters had predicted April output would rise, with forecasts ranging from a 0.3 percent to a 1.5 percent increase, compared with a month-on-month drop of 0.3 percent in March. "Those who had sold earlier on fears that interest rates may rise sooner than expected were busy covering their shorts after the data," said an analyst at the securities affiliate of another city bank.
"This was because the output figures showed the timing of a discount rate rise may not be as early as July, although it may come some time this year," he said.
The Trade Ministry also said that manufacturers' output was expected to rise 2.7 percent in May from the previous month, but to fall 1.9 percent in June.

After a brief rally, the June JGB futures stabilised. The key contract was at 123.45 at 0518 GMT, against Wednesday's 122.90 close. The yield of the 182nd 10-year JGB fell to 2.620 percent, down 0.065 from Wednesday.
